items.title: 67425_Tiny Grimes oral history interview
items.q: And he would take it from there, and Slam would take his part.

ctx.x: So you would talk things over until you got it together.

Yeah, It didn't take too many times, you know. Just 2 or 3 times to find out where each riff should be or where I should come in after his solos, or how many bars that I would take -- how long I would play. And he would take it from there, and Slam would take his part. It's very interesting [the recording]. First time I've heard it, you know lately.
Do you remember doing these tunes? If I had you, Japanese Sandman, Soft Winds.

items.title: 67849_Leroy Elliot Stewart oral history interview
items.q: Along with myself, Tiny Grimes was on guitar. And we had quite a few rehearsals, every chance we got.

ctx.x: Now, did you -- did he like to work out the kinds of progressions that you all were to play or did he just -- did you all rehearse much or did he just --
Yes, we rehearsed quite a bit. Along with myself, Tiny Grimes was on guitar. And we had quite a few rehearsals, every chance we got.
You rehearsed a lot. What kinds of things did you work out in rehearsals, do you remember?
